$comment: Isolates defect 3: the in-sim gossip path does not reach the answer the same kernel produces offline.

Gossip and the coordinator cascade are the SAME algorithm - gossip.py's own docstring says it reuses the closed-form (z, sigma) cell update from kernel.py and is 'same answer, no coordinator'. Only the realisation differs: x_bar is rebuilt from peers' broadcast x_i (a peer that misses iter_timeout_s is held over at its LAST-SEEN x_i, so the iterate runs on stale data), and the round is bounded on the CARRIER (sim) clock at round_timeout_s / iter_timeout_s = 2.0/0.2 = ~10 iterations TOTAL shared across all 4 tiers, against admm_max_iters=200 PER TIER for the replicated path.

Measured motivation, el_dependent: solving the cascade offline on the campaign's own published B (B_el=0.4422, B_heat=0.3518, B_gas=0.4329) with the real 21xP2H + 26xCHP fleet gives P2H=1.000 CHP=0.408 = 0.174 MW of CP heat, at 3 iterations/tier and at convergence alike. The sim delivers 0.005-0.024 MW and logs cp_priority_admm mean_factor=0.057. So the kernel is not being clamped downstream - the gossip realisation is landing somewhere else.

Arms separate PROTOCOL from BUDGET: 'lexicographic' removes both the message staleness and the iteration cap; 'gossip_long' keeps gossip and only quadruples the round budget (8.0/0.2 = ~40 iterations). If gossip_long recovers most of the gap it is the budget; if only lexicographic does, it is the stale x_bar.
Both accounting fixes (enable_cp_slack_headroom / enable_cp_own_supply_netting) are ON in every arm - this campaign is about the realisation, not the books.
Judge on: outcomes__cp_generation n_active/heat_mw/gas_mw against the 0.174 MW offline target, served_by_sector heat/gas fraction, PWSF, and the n_active SPREAD across seeds.
name: ab_cp_gossip_vs_lexicographic
